AngloGold Ashanti Obuasi Mine has received multiple honours at the 10th edition of the Sustainability and Social Investment (SSI) Awards, including the SSI Foundation Company of the Year award.
The Mine also secured several corporate awards, while its Managing Director, Dr Ing. Sam Pobee, and Director of Sustainability Management, Edmund Oduro Agyei, received individual recognitions.
Dr Pobee was named SSI Impact CEO of the Year for his leadership and commitment to responsible mining, sustainability and socio-economic development.
Mr Oduro Agyei received the Sustainability Professional of the Year award for his work in advancing the Mine’s sustainability agenda through community development, strategic partnerships, economic empowerment and social investment.
Commenting on the recognition, Mr Oduro Agyei said the awards reflected the collective efforts of the Mine, its employees, development partners and host communities.
He linked the achievements to investments under the Mine’s Socio-Economic Development Plan (SEDP 2022–2031), which he said had contributed to improving livelihoods, strengthening local economies and expanding access to essential social services.
He dedicated the awards to the Sustainability Management team and other stakeholders involved in advancing the Mine’s development agenda.

Two other employees received individual honours. Phylis Quainoo was presented with the Diversity and Inclusion Leadership Impact Award, while Daniel Arthur Bentum received the Mentorship Leadership Impact Award.
The recognitions cover areas including healthcare, education, community infrastructure, local enterprise development, gender inclusion and environmental protection.
The Mine says its social investment programmes are intended to support socio-economic development in its host communities beyond its mining operations.
